oxabolone.text: Oxabolone is a nandrolone-family anabolic steroid that appears in muscle-building discussions as one of the obscure compounds in that class, with users associating it with lean mass gain. Almost nothing is published on it, so its use for physique rests on its chemical family and anecdote.

sm-130686.text: SM-130686 is an oral growth hormone secretagogue that gets mentioned in muscle and anti-aging circles because raising growth hormone is linked to leaner, fuller-looking physiques. It is known from lab and animal papers; its muscle or appearance effects in people are untested.

bezafibrate.text: Bezafibrate is a lipid-lowering drug that comes up in fat-loss forums because it acts on the same PPAR-delta pathway as compounds like GW501516, so some posters treat it as a related fat-burning option. Its use for body composition is untested and based on that association.

seladelpar.text: Seladelpar is an approved PPAR-delta agonist for a liver condition. Fat-loss circles discuss it only because it shares a target with GW501516, which is promoted for endurance and leanness. Its use for body composition is untested; the approved studies concern liver disease.

elafibranor.text: Elafibranor is an approved dual PPAR-alpha/delta agonist for a liver condition. It is mentioned in fat-loss discussion because PPAR-delta activation is linked to greater fat burning, though its appearance or fat-loss effects have not been studied.

gw0742.text: GW0742 is a research PPAR-delta agonist sold gray-market as a "Cardarine 2.0", and users take it in cutting phases hoping for greater fat burning and endurance. The evidence for that use is lab and animal data; human physique trials have not been run.

l-165041.text: L-165041 is a lab PPAR-delta agonist that appears in fat-loss and endurance discussions as another member of the GW501516 family, with users linking the pathway to greater fat burning and leanness. Evidence comes from cell and mouse studies; human fat-loss data are lacking.

acadesine.text: Acadesine (AICAR) is promoted in fat-loss and performance circles as an exercise mimetic, with users hoping for greater fat burning without extra training. The idea comes from a 2008 mouse study; human fat-loss effects have not been shown.

slu-pp-332.text: SLU-PP-332 is billed in fat-loss circles as an exercise mimetic that could deliver leanness and endurance gains without extra training. The basis is mouse research showing exercise-like gene activity and less fat gain; human data do not exist.

bam-15.text: BAM15 is traded online as a "safer DNP", with users hoping to raise calorie burn and shed fat for a leaner look. The evidence is from mouse studies showing fat loss; human effects have not been tested.

adipotide.text: Adipotide is discussed in fat-loss forums as a peptide that targets the blood supply of fat tissue to shrink it. Its weight loss was shown in obese monkeys, while human data are absent and development stopped.

fenfluramine.text: Fenfluramine was a widely used prescription appetite suppressant, often combined with phentermine as fen-phen, and is cited in diet-drug history as a strong weight-loss option. Its weight-loss effect was studied in trials, and it was withdrawn in 1997; it is now an epilepsy medicine.

ephedrine-caffeine-eca-stack.text: The ECA stack is a classic cutting aid in bodybuilding circles, used to boost energy and fat loss while dieting for a leaner, more defined physique. Trials have found modest fat-loss effects, mostly alongside diet and exercise.

zenagamtide.text: Zenagamtide (amycretin) is a not-yet-approved dual GLP-1/amylin drug followed closely in fat-loss circles because early trials reported large weight-loss figures. Evidence is from early-stage trials in obesity; its use for cosmetic leanness has not been studied.

enicepatide.text: Enicepatide is Roche's investigational weekly GLP-1/GIP dual agonist, watched by weight-loss followers as a possible rival to tirzepatide. It is in phase 3 trials for obesity; appearance-focused use has not been studied.

ct-996.text: CT-996 is an experimental oral GLP-1 pill from Roche, followed by fat-loss communities interested in a non-injectable alternative to semaglutide-type drugs. It has registered phase 2 trials and no published results, so its weight-loss effect is untested.

petrelintide.text: Petrelintide is a weekly amylin analogue from Zealand and Roche, discussed in fat-loss circles as part of the next wave of obesity drugs beyond GLP-1. It is in phase 3 for weight management; its appearance effects specifically have not been studied.

eloralintide.text: Eloralintide is Lilly's weekly amylin agonist, followed by fat-loss communities because phase 2 trials reported roughly 9 to 20 percent weight loss at 48 weeks. It is unapproved, and use for cosmetic leanness has not been studied.

maridebart-cafraglutide.text: MariTide is Amgen's monthly injection discussed in fat-loss circles for its less frequent dosing and roughly 12-16% weight loss at a year in phase 2. It is in phase 3, and appearance-focused outcomes have not been studied.

aleniglipron.text: Aleniglipron is an experimental once-daily GLP-1 pill that fat-loss followers watch as a non-injectable option, with phase 2b trials showing about 8-11% placebo-adjusted weight loss over 36 weeks. Its use for cosmetic leanness has not been studied.

accg-2671.text: ACCG-2671 is an early oral amylin agonist for obesity that appears in pipeline-watching fat-loss discussion. Its only public record is a first-in-human trial registration, so its weight-loss effect has not been shown.

elecoglipron.text: Elecoglipron is AstraZeneca's once-daily GLP-1 pill, followed by fat-loss communities for its convenience and phase 2 weight loss of up to about 10% at 26 weeks. Phase 3 is under way, and appearance-focused outcomes have not been studied.

azd6234.text: AZD6234 is AstraZeneca's long-acting amylin agonist injection for obesity, noted in fat-loss pipeline discussion. Phase 3 is registered but no efficacy results are published, so its weight-loss effect is untested in public data.

azd9550.text: AZD9550 is an experimental GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist from AstraZeneca, discussed by fat-loss followers because glucagon activity is linked to extra calorie burn. It is tested alone and with an amylin agonist, with no published results yet.

berobenatide.text: Berobenatide is Pfizer's investigational monthly GLP-1 agonist, noted in fat-loss pipeline discussion for its dosing frequency. Only phase 3 registrations exist, so its weight-loss effect is untested in public data.

pf-08653945.text: PF-08653945 is Pfizer's early-stage amylin analogue for weight management, appearing in fat-loss pipeline discussion. Nothing has been published on its effects, so its link to leanness is untested.

abbv-295.text: ABBV-295 is AbbVie's injectable amylin analogue for obesity, noted in fat-loss pipeline discussion. It is in early trials with no results out, so its weight-loss effect is untested in public data.

pramlintide.text: Pramlintide is an approved diabetes drug that fat-loss circles discuss because weight loss appears alongside its blood sugar effects and it is an amylin analogue like newer obesity drugs. Weight loss was observed in diabetes trials; use for cosmetic leanness is off-label.

dulaglutide.text: Dulaglutide is a weekly GLP-1 diabetes drug that some fat-loss followers view as an older relative of semaglutide, taken for lower appetite and modest weight loss. Weight loss was seen in diabetes trials; it is not approved for obesity.

lixisenatide.text: Lixisenatide is a short-acting daily GLP-1 diabetes drug that appears in fat-loss discussion mainly as an older member of the GLP-1 class. Small weight reductions were seen in diabetes trials, and it plays a minor role compared with newer agents.
